---
title: "11. Monte Carlo and yield"
subtitle: "Explore a distribution without losing failed samples"
julia:
  env: ["JULIA_PROJECT=../../../AmberMakie/docs"]
---

```{julia}
#| include: false
using Pkg
Pkg.activate(joinpath(@__DIR__, "../../../AmberMakie/docs"))
using Amber, AmberMakie, CairoMakie
using Random, Statistics
CairoMakie.activate!()
set_theme!(theme_amber_light())
```

Monte Carlo analysis turns component tolerances into a distribution of a
design metric. Here the metric is the DC output of a resistive divider and the
two resistor values vary independently.

```{julia}
@circuit MakieRandomDivider() begin
    gnd = ground()
    input = node()
    output = node()
    Source = voltage_source(input, gnd; dc=1V)
    Rtop = resistor(input, output; value=10kΩ)
    Rbottom = resistor(output, gnd; value=10kΩ)
end

metric(result) = only(voltage(result, :output))
ensemble = monte_carlo(MakieRandomDivider(); samples=300, seed=2026,
    variations=Dict(
        Symbol("Rtop.value") => Gaussian(10kΩ, 500Ω),
        Symbol("Rbottom.value") => Gaussian(10kΩ, 500Ω),
    ),
    metric=metric);
```

`ensembleplot` shows the metric distribution, while `correlationplot` answers
which varied parameter drives it. Failed simulations remain represented in
AmberMakie rather than silently disappearing from the study.

```{julia}
figure = Figure(size=(1150, 560))
ensembleplot(figure[1, 1], ensemble;
    metric=:output_voltage, bins=28, color="#0072B2")
correlationplot(figure[1, 2], ensemble;
    parameter=Symbol("Rtop.value"), metric=:output_voltage,
    color=(:black, 0.30), markersize=6)
Label(figure[0, :], "Divider output across component variation"; fontsize=20)
figure
```

## Turn the distribution into a specification

Suppose the output must remain between 0.47 V and 0.53 V. `yieldplot` displays
the pass/fail split, and the Julia cell computes the exact yield printed below
it.

```{julia}
yield_figure = Figure(size=(800, 500))
yieldplot(yield_figure[1, 1], ensemble; limits=0.47 => 0.53)
Label(yield_figure[0, 1], "Yield for 0.50 V ± 30 mV"; fontsize=20)
yield_figure
```

```{julia}
values = Float64[value for value in ensemble.values if value !== nothing]
passed = count(value -> 0.47 <= value <= 0.53, values)

(
    converged=length(values),
    failed=count(!, ensemble.converged),
    mean_voltage=mean(values),
    standard_deviation=std(values),
    yield_percent=100passed / length(values),
)
```

Because the seed and every sampled parameter set are stored in the result, a
surprising sample can be selected and replayed in the Monte Carlo workbench.
